description: Alarm response, schedules, setpoints, trend review, and preventive maintenance of the BAS at city hall, the library, and the community center
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: City contract: critical alarms acknowledged within 1 hour and worked within 4 hours, 24x7; a library or city hall closure for heat follows within a day in summer; CT-C is about 64% of receipts. RPO set by how often programs and schedules change (weekly at most)
manual_workaround: Field controllers keep running their last programs and schedules without the supervisory controller or the owner; the city maintenance worker can put air handlers in hand mode at the panel with the owner on the phone; printed one-page manual operation sheet per building (to be written, P01 R-006)
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-02; SYS-03; SYS-04; SYS-08 (city BAS through the city VPN)
dependent_third_parties: City IT (VPN and identity provider); controls distributor (parts)
dependent_people_or_facilities: Owner (single point of failure; the only BAS technician the city has); city maintenance worker; work van

description: Cardholder adds and removals, door schedules, holiday schedules, and emergency lock or unlock requests in the city's cloud access control tenant
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Badge removals must be done within 4 business hours of the city's request (a departed employee keeps building access until then); a wrong door schedule leaves doors unlocked or blocks staff; RPO set by the monthly cardholder export and door schedule copies kept by the owner (the tenant itself is backed up by the access control vendor for the city)
manual_workaround: City IT manager is the second tenant administrator and can disable a badge; door controllers keep enforcing their cached schedules and credentials if the cloud service is down; physical keys held by the city facilities manager
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-02; SYS-03; SYS-08 (access control tenant through the city identity provider)
dependent_third_parties: Access control SaaS vendor (the city's vendor); city IT (identity provider)

description: Programming changes, troubleshooting, and sequence checks on GSA's BAS at the federal building, worked on site on the GSA-furnished workstation
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Subcontract: on site within 1 business day of a call; the prime has its own technicians for urgent work; GSA systems are not on the owner's devices, so an outage of the owner's IT does not stop this work as long as the owner, the PIV card, and the van are available
manual_workaround: Prime contractor's building engineers cover urgent work; work orders can be read on the phone or printed at the prime's site office
dependent_systems: SYS-02 (work orders and FCI); SYS-03; SYS-09 (GSA workstation and BSN, outside the boundary)
dependent_third_parties: Prime contractor; GSA (PIV card, workstation, BSN)
dependent_people_or_facilities: Owner; GSA PIV card; federal building

description: Monthly invoices to the city and the prime, payments, insurance certificates, and contract records
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $15,000 is invoiced a month; the city pays net 30 and the prime net 45, so a week's delay costs nothing but cash flow; personal savings cover about two months of expenses
manual_workaround: Invoices can be issued from a spreadsheet template and sent from the phone; contract records also on paper in the home office
dependent_third_parties: Accounting SaaS provider; the owner's bank

description: Email and phone with the city and the prime, alarm emails and texts, drawings and records in cloud storage
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: BAS alarms arrive by email and email-to-text, so a lost phone or email account delays BP-01; contract notices (city 24 hours, prime immediately) need a working phone and email; cloud storage keeps file versions
manual_workaround: Phone calls from any phone; the city facilities manager and the prime's project manager have the owner's number; printed contact list (P08)
dependent_people_or_facilities: Owner (all credentials and the only MFA device)
